previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and opioid dependence was admitted after a fall during alcohol relapse. He presented with knee, back, and shoulder pain, acute alcohol intoxication, and wheezing suggestive of an asthma exacerbation. Initial evaluation ruled out fractures and intracranial injury. He was diagnosed with alcohol withdrawal syndrome and started on a Librium taper, with no complications. His asthma was managed with a steroid burst and bronchodilators. Abdominal pain was attributed to opioid withdrawal, improved with methadone restart. Imaging confirmed cirrhosis and portal hypertension with reversed portal flow and splenomegaly, but no acute findings. Liver enzymes trended downward, and he remained stable. He was discharged home on his prior medications with referrals to outpatient programs and specialist follow-up.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
Other diseases of stomach and duodenum

Brief Hospital Course:
___ male history of alcohol abuse, asthma, cirrhosis, 
complicated by esophageal gastric varices presents with alcohol 
intoxication 

#ETOH Withdrawal. Patient with a history of severe withdrawal 
symptoms and seizures requiring phenobarbital in the past. 
Initially presented with tachycardia, tremors, and formication 
with BAL of 455 on admission. He was treated with Ativan per 
CIWA scale and with high dose thiamine, folate, and a 
multivitamin. Symptoms improved by day of discharge. Social work 
met with the patient and he reports that he Sectioned 35 himself 
recently and spent 33 days in a facility in ___. He states 
he was sober for 1 week after. He states that he is not 
interested in AA and prefers to go to church as part of his 
treatment for his ETOH use.

#Abdominal pain. Patient with history of chronic abdominal pain 
and pancreatitis. Lipase within normal limits on arrival. CT A/P 
was reassuring against an acute process and abdominal ultrasound 
with dopplers was negative for thrombosis. Abdominal pain is 
likely musculoskeletal in etiology as he reports falling on his 
abdomen while intoxicated and he was subsequently treated with 
oxycodone PRN and Lidocaine patch.

#Tachycardia. Initially in sinus tachycardia to the 110s that 
persisted throughout his hospitalization. Patient reported 
associated pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. Given 
his history of PE in ___ and Wells score of 3, decision was 
made to pursue CTA chest which did not reveal PE. Sinus 
tachycardia was subsequently felt to be related to his abdominal 
pain (see above) and anxiety (in the setting of ETOH withdrawal) 
which were treated as described above. 

#Alcoholic Cirrhosis. Previous history of hepatic 
encephalopathy, gastric varices. He was continued on home 
torsemide, spironolactone, and lactulose. 

#Opioid dependence. Patient with history of dilaudid use/abuse 
and was recently at detox and discharged on suboxone, which he 
is no longer taking and does not desire to continue.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
===================
[ ] Met with social work about his ETOH use. He did not seem to 
express motivation to stop drinking, and states that his high 
BAL was the result of drinking over several days. He did accept 
resource info around relapse prevention programs in his area. 
Continue to encourage abstaining from ETOH use and participation 
in such resources that would aid with discontinuation.
[ ] Patient is at high risk for opioid and ETOH dependence vs 
withdrawal. He is at high risk for relapse.

===================

coordination.
